edbDesc: (also known as solid electrolytes and superionic conductors) Solid state electrical conductors which conduct due to the movement of ions through voids (or empty crystallographic positions)in their crystal lattice. One component of the structure, cationic or anionic, is essentially free to move throughout the structure, acting as charge carrier.
title: Fast Ion Conductor
pickWhy: Borderline: Faraday found that solid lead fluoride and silver sulfide conduct electricity by moving ions in his 1833-34 electrolysis researches, the same work as the Laws of electrolysis card; borderline because it is now a big field of its own (solid-state batteries, car oxygen sensors, solid oxide fuel cells), so it could be its own card. I picked attach.
